path: Try one card → optional Quick start
decision: A hands-on reveal/rate demonstration precedes creation/import. Quick start is optional. Existing welcome decks and history are preserved.
verification: First-run browser demo checked in the prior onboarding pass; existing installs are not overwritten.

decision: The same full-screen name step leads directly to a full-screen first card. Focus starts in the name field, then Front. Keep creation visible until the editor and database are ready; render the initial blank draft before first paint.
verification: Fresh first-run browser walkthrough: name focus, Back, creation, full 390×844 editor, clean close. Required fields and guarded dirty dismissal checked in library creation.

decision: Short compatibility label retained. Cancelling leaves onboarding in place; an invalid chosen file reaches a visible error with creation/import choices still available.
verification: Invalid first-run import and valid retry browser checked; native Files permissions not exercised.

decision: Make cards / Import Anki remain primary. Search, Settings and Add use three bottom utility controls. Imported tags and contextual tagging are preserved; no global Tags catalogue entry. Bottom mode dots appear only with decks.
verification: Source reviewed; empty-library import recovery was checked earlier.

decision: A full-screen creation page uses ivory/green paper drawings and serif italics. No boxed blue/green options. Back from the name returns to choices with the draft intact; Back from choices returns to the library.
verification: Browser checked at 390px: full viewport, name preserved across Back, Escape steps back, cancellation creates no deck. Import picker and failure notice exercised.

decision: Deck rows and counts derive directly from the registry. Removed the extra copied state that could briefly show an empty library.
verification: Saved manual deck and photo survived browser reload; imported image rendered in Study.

path: Open Anki file before onboarding is complete
decision: A file arriving from Files already expresses the user’s choice. Bypass first-run choices and wait for database readiness before consuming it.
verification: Source reviewed; native Open in handoff still requires a physical-device test. A file arriving during an existing study route remains queued until the library opens.

decision: Retain the two existing library modes and bottom dots, with no visible mode switch/names. A swipe needs sufficient distance, brisk pace and a clearly horizontal direction. Tiny flicks, slow long drags and outer-edge gestures return. The gesture still translates one list rather than showing a second page halfway.
verification: 21 pure intent tests cover valid directions, tiny/slow/diagonal movement, invalid input and screen widths. Click guard resets on a fresh press. Physical gesture feel needs owner confirmation. The separate deck-row navigation study remains unshipped.

decision: Tap studies the deck; a single ellipsis opens Manage deck. Empty decks open their first card. Removed the decorative folio beside names in the library and deck headers; optional real cover images remain.
verification: Browser checked on the saved demo deck.

decision: iPhone uses native UISearchBar. An active-only transparent UIKit control above WebKit owns the first outside press, closes field and keyboard, and consumes that press; focus-end cleanup is a guarded fallback. Native Search submits without clearing results. Outside collapse retains the query, with a quiet dot and accessible Filter active marker on Search; X explicitly clears/closes. Browser has matching query retention and 180ms collapse; native collapse 220ms. Add/Settings and blocking imports clear search state. Explicit native open/closed events include the current query.
verification: Owner confirmed repaired native outside dismissal on iPhone. Browser checked retained filter, reopen with the same query, explicit clear and creation first-tap behavior. Native source review covered layering and submit/end-editing cleanup; UIKit retains query ownership even after collapse to reject stale web echoes. Final updated build installed in place; rapid typing/reopen retention still needs physical confirmation.

decision: Single-line names; full names remain readable and selectable.
verification: Browser checked earlier

decision: One route contains cards and deck details. Name changes use explicit Save; Back protects an unsaved name. Cover and Restore media stay here.
verification: Management entry and unsaved-name protection browser checked. Name persistence/rollback has database regression coverage.

decision: Activity returns to Manage deck Details rather than losing context in the library.
verification: Route reviewed; earlier statistics calculations remain covered by regression tests.

decision: Controls edit a draft. Save commits one complete update; Back offers Keep editing / Discard. Existing card schedules/history are not rewritten.
verification: Browser change → discard → reopen retained the original value. SQL regressions cover validation, failed persistence rollback and preserved state/history.

decision: Cards only and Cards & study history live in one collapsed Export section.
verification: Callbacks preserved; final native share-sheet handoff remains a phone check.

verification: Source reviewed. No user deck deletion was performed.

decision: Keep both leads. Replacement remains explicit about cards and study history. Native modal focuses the safe action and Escape cancels; multi-deck replacement remains unavailable.
verification: Browser cancellation preserved the existing deck; parser/rollback tests pass. Replacement not executed.

decision: Kept actionable errors instead of a false import success.
verification: Source reviewed

decision: One visible face, one working area and one tool strip. Other-face drafts stay mounted. Tags/audio/deletion are secondary.
verification: Both side drafts, existing photo, ordering and Save retained through the browser walkthrough.

decision: One explicit Save action for both new and existing cards. Study returns to the same face without rating or advancing.

decision: Inline shared confirmation replaces the extra discard popup. Keep editing restores the working area; destructive section/card/deck decisions use the same safe-first pattern.
verification: Dirty Back and Keep editing/Save browser checked. Native keyboard behaviour remains open.

decision: Kept for finding or managing large decks. Bulk delete stays behind selection and confirmation.

path: Question ↔ answer → Again / Hard / Good / Easy
decision: Small written-card and eye faces replace the numbered caption. Either side can be revisited without rating or advancing. Side controls pause during committed rating feedback. Recall labels now use .72 opacity and return-time estimates .9, keeping the art visually primary.
verification: Browser checked: repeated flips preserve the question and queue progress; Enter/Space; 44px targets; long-question portrait/landscape layout. Native VoiceOver not exercised.

decision: A static lower-edge fade and small downward cue appear only when more content remains below. No idle animation or live blur. Both faces retain their own scrolling across flips; new content starts at the top. Recall art and touch areas are slightly larger, bounded by each button's width. Latest refinement: the fade covers the last 28px; a smaller, lower eye leaves more room for the question. Card tags follow the answer content rather than overlaying pictures.
verification: Browser checked long imported image → scroll to bottom → cue disappears; short Practice card has no cue. Choice layout checked at 320×568, 390/440px portrait and 812×375 landscape. No physical battery measurement.

decision: 450ms stationary hold plus 90ms pixel feedback offers Edit this side. Tapping it opens that face without focusing text. Direct Edit/F2 remains an explicit alternative. Opening does not change the card; Save remains required.
verification: Browser holds verified on question and answer. Tapping away dismisses without flipping; the editor opens with Back focused and Save disabled. Updated iPhone build installed; physical hold/keyboard confirmation remains.

decision: No early-review quantity picker. Continuing opens free practice without changing schedules. Next-session timing includes learning and relearning cards.
verification: Browser checked

decision: The same reversible face control works in library Practice and post-study Practice. Only Again or Put aside changes the session queue. Feedback is owned by the session, so changing face cannot cancel a committed choice. Both routes share the quieter .72-opacity action captions used in Study and onboarding.
verification: Browser checked in both Practice routes: return to the same question, repeat resets to front, Put aside advances and completion still works.

decision: Shared finish design. Done returns to the library without another completion screen.

decision: Real Study, Practice and review-again cards share a finger-controlled perspective plane. Choose scrolling or horizontal turning once at 12px, favouring scrolling on diagonals; full-turn travel is 80% of starting width capped at 360px. Short unrevealed turns cancel. First answer exposure registers the session reveal once before painting it; reversing/cancelling still settles to the nearest answer orientation. Separate later gestures/face buttons can return to the question. Preserve independent face scroll, original content/art, direct alternatives and one flip haptic, with ratings/schedules changed only by explicit recall choices. Respect Reduce Motion; no idle loop.
verification: Owner confirmed iPhone drag and selection-free hold work after the capture/scroller repair. Latest sensitivity and reveal-latch tuning: 306 tests, full lint, TypeScript, web and signed native builds pass; installed and launched in place. Controller checks cover peek/reverse/release/cancel once, no long spin, permanent vertical lock, slow vertical click suppression, captured width and native capture transfer. Browser checked short cancel, vertical movement, shorter deliberate flip, question return and hold lock. Final phone feel remains an owner check; review-again completion-only route remains source checked.

path: Hold current face → progress → Edit or X → selectable editor
decision: Suppress study selection/callouts. A 116px sparse pixel stitch fills outside the thumb over the hold, then acknowledges once with a light haptic. Dim the locked card and offer a contrasting cut-corner paper ticket with italic Edit and a separate X. Freeze card movement and other actions until Edit or X; Back/Escape cancel. Existing-card editing opens without a keyboard. Photo/video Add, Paste and Arrange → Copy belong inside the editor, with durable storage and busy guards.
verification: Owner confirmed the selection/hold lock repair. Browser checked the larger cue geometry, contrasting ticket in Light/black, front/back offers and correct-back editor with Back focus/Save disabled. Previous photo/video checks remain; no card/rating edits saved in this pass. 312 tests and web/native builds pass. Actual thumb visibility, clipboard permission/round-trip and haptic feel remain phone checks. Binary cross-device sync remains incomplete.

decision: Slow deliberate swipes switch by distance with no hidden speed/deadline veto. Keep initial horizontal intent through later vertical drift; normal vertical scrolling never switches pages. Resist and cap displacement to 48px inward/12px outward. Two separate 44px dot targets stay fixed; a 3px pip travels through the gap and fades before either dot, without overlapping. Keep no visible mode names or extra switch; Reduce Motion uses static dots.
verification: 31 targeted math tests plus controller lifecycle checks cover slow drags, outer bounds, locked intent, marker/commit agreement, long vertical click suppression and fresh touches interrupting return. Browser measured separate 44px targets/4px anchors. Full 312 tests and web/native builds pass. This Mac uses Reduce Motion; continuous phone touch motion remains an owner check.

decision: Remove Click 2 see from the actual reveal control and onboarding. Keep an accessible Show answer name. Study retains its emerald eye and spaced outward rays; Practice uses lapis/platinum with a close broken orbit in both free-practice routes. No visible top mode names or switch.
verification: Browser compared production art in Light/black and checked actual Practice front/back; Study control retains its original eye. 312 tests and production/native builds pass. Distinguishability and subtle motion still need owner feedback on the phone.

decision: Use one StudyFooter action area and 44px control row in all three session routes, with balanced side slots, no row margins and one shared bottom safe-area inset. Preserve Study Undo and anchor its previous-card arrow to the physical bottom-left corner, with at least 16px edge padding plus safe-area protection. Landscape reserves space below the card for that target.
verification: Reproduced and repaired the 4px Study answer-side jump; prior checks found zero vertical drift at 393×852, 320×568, 667×375 and 400×688, with all paper targets 44×44px. Latest corner-placement check: arrow left16/bottom16 at 400×688 and left16/bottom18 at 667×375, unchanged front/back; landscape content ends before its target. No card/rating edits saved. Review-again shares the same component but its completion entry was source checked. The prior full suite passed 312 tests; this placement-only update passed lint, TypeScript and web/signed native builds. Installed and launched in place on the iPhone.

decision: Preserve authored pixels, colours and animation timing while compiling the eye into nine colour paths and each icon border into only exposed boundary loops. Remove hidden interior strokes; keep the thin rounded black contour.
verification: Five geometry tests prove production fill and boundary preservation; 15 targeted compiler/turn tests, lint, TypeScript and web/signed native builds pass. Both eye variants have zero rectangles, nine colour paths and one contour loop. Installed in place; automatic launch was denied because the phone was locked. Structural savings are verified; battery savings are not measured.

path: Rapid reveal / next → native crash and energy validation
decision: Keep the native scrolling-layer exception open until its trigger is reproducible. Reconcile the iOS15 deployment setting with newer browser assumptions, then validate older physical devices. Prioritize decoded-image sizing, bounded deck/media caches and coalesced sync work.
verification: Retrieved a pre-outline-update SIGABRT report in UIScrollView pan/contentOffset/CALayer bounds; this report is not a memory kill. Owner's subsequent 30sec rapid-card run did not reproduce it. A short connected development trace measured WebContent footprint up to ~203MiB, but uncontrolled interaction state and no paired power trace prevent idle/battery-life or improvement claims. Geometry optimization does not close this crash.

decision: Crossfade only the action artwork over150ms; leave card turning and the bottom face tools unchanged. Retain one front/back action set, make the inactive set inert/aria-hidden/pointer-disabled immediately and pause its animations. No state delay or new idle loop; Reduce Motion swaps immediately.
verification: Explicit sample observed both opacity transitions end at150ms in either direction. Actual Study/Practice expose only current actions; Study paper targets remain y628 on both faces at400×688. No card/rating edits saved. Review-again uses the shared footer in source. Lint, TypeScript and web/signed native builds pass. Separate native scrolling crash remains open.

path: Fast mixed-direction card gestures → interrupted turn
decision: Keep the last flat card/footer geometry stable through dragging and interrupted springs; release geometry only after flat paint. Preserve immediate answer registration and control state. Cancel pending hold without focus during a pan; recover expected pointer-capture cancellation.
verification: 12,000 controller interruption trials plus layout/focus/capture-recovery checks pass. Full lint, TypeScript, 360 tests and web/signed iOS builds pass. Installed and launched in place on the iPhone. Owner repeated mixed-direction swipes and reported no freeze. Earlier native scrolling crash remains open; owner separately reported excessive elastic edge travel and a one-time reveal-control resize.

path: First answer exposure → lifetime counter and session record
decision: Count the first reveal of a stable queue occurrence in Study and Practice. Retain independent lifetime and session records, display only a small lifetime ×N by the face controls. Repeated side toggles, edits, Undo and callback retries do not inflate it. Local journal recovery is separate from scheduling; dirty-only cloud mirroring reuses existing sync events.
verification: 35 storage/merge/platform tests plus eight UI-coordinator tests cover recovery, dedupe, startup failure, offline retry and concurrent upload. Data-free footer preview checked in small portrait/landscape; no actual test-card ratings or counts saved. Installed on iPhone; owner confirmed count works and repeated front/back flipping does not inflate it. Counts start with this update, are not included in current Anki scheduling exports, and cross-device sync has no two-physical-device validation yet.

decision: Give retained eye and rating layers independent final-size canvases anchored above the fixed face tools. Preserve frozen card geometry during a drag/spring and immediate reveal registration. Short landscape uses the same card-left/actions-right grid on both faces.
verification: Reproduced eye174→106.5px and84px rating jump; browser now measures zero eye/rating/tool drift across both mismatch states at440×956,393×852,320×568 and667×375. Short/long/late-image samples and Practice checked without real history writes.366 tests and web/signed native builds pass; installed and launched in place on the iPhone; owner confirmed controls stay steady on reveal/return.

verification: Six math/intent tests and a lifecycle harness cover edge/reversal/release/cancel, zero-offset cleanup, interrupted input and interaction guards. Browser long-text reaches its real bottom and late images update the cue without moving controls.
